items.title: Link anonymous thread and turn lifecycle events
items.body:
## Human comments

## What was wrong

Work events cannot reliably connect an accepted message to its turn, especially after queueing or retry.

## What changed

- Persist random analytics-only thread, parent, and message IDs separately from content and public thread records.
- Report applied lifecycle transitions and coarse turn outcomes after commit, retaining queue groups and original acceptance timestamps.
- Reuse retry provenance, exclude steering from turn origins, and report unavailable links without guessing.
- Restrict new turn outcome provider values to shipped declarations, including after custom providers are disabled.

## How you verified

- [Remote CI passed](https://github.com/get-bb/bb/actions/runs/38452449814) at `a96641c3e8`.
- ACP-next ran uncached in the sequential Windows host shard; its original tests and timeouts are unchanged.
- Real Codex root, child, follow-up, and grouped queued turns completed through the branch app/server/daemon.
- Thread, parent, and request IDs joined correctly; archiving emitted the expected lifecycle transition.
- A real Claude rejection using an isolated invalid OAuth token emitted `failed/auth`.
- A due one-shot automation completed with `trigger: schedule`, using the same turn events as other work.
- Production-sender payloads were captured locally and screened for identifying content; no production PostHog delivery occurred.
- The older Claude error path without an HTTP status remains a separate categorization limitation.
- Cumulative verification used `207404a8b7`; the later #5439 fix changes only plugin RPC request metadata.

<details>
<summary>Prior implementation verification and review history</summary>

- [Remote CI passed](https://github.com/get-bb/bb/actions/runs/38394027310) at `41e9b51b`.
- [Privacy regressions failed before the fix](https://github.com/get-bb/bb/actions/runs/38393587802) and passed afterward on Linux and Windows.
- Cumulative review covered the stack at `654570f7`; its provider privacy finding is fixed and validated without repeating the review.
- Exact-head app/server/daemon → deterministic ACP process → local capture verified root/child IDs, continuation, queued sends, stop, opt-out, restart persistence, and a disabled custom provider mapping to `other`.
- A grouped queued send on the unchanged descendant `40972c58` emitted both accepted message IDs on `turn_started` and `turn_finished`. The original QA request used an incomplete expected queue prefix; correcting that fixture request completed the check.
- Retry, steer, permission, and failure variants are covered in remote CI rather than every variant in the live pass.

<details>
<summary>Recorded P2 follow-ups</summary>

- Soft deletion can clear analytics state before final runtime settlement; startup cancellation can lose the pending request link.
- Retained-turn reconciliation can count another start; host interruption can be categorized as `start_failed`.
- `first_turn` uses current root-thread count rather than historical first completion.
- Request-origin lookup scans historical request JSON.

</details>

</details>

Original implementation thread: [Retention measurement](https://brsbl.getbb.app/projects/proj_khiw2za95v/threads/thr_gqshddt6w2)

items.title: Pi: injected AskUserQuestion interaction stays pending with no card, then times out after 30 minutes

labels.name: no-repro
labels.description: Could not reproduce as reported (or already fixed); see linked report

items.body:
### Summary

On a visible Pi thread, BB's injected `AskUserQuestion` registered a plugin interaction and the
agent's turn ended normally, but no question card ever appeared in the desktop app. The interaction
sat `pending` for exactly 30 minutes, then became `interrupted` with `statusReason: timeout`. The
user saw only the collapsed `Worked for` row and the agent's "Waiting on your pick" line, and said
later there was nothing to pick.

### Versions and environment

- bb 0.45.0 (desktop AppImage), Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic
- provider `pi`, Pi CLI 1.0.2
- builtin plugin `ask-user-question@0.1.0` (running)
- visible project thread `thr_7c3mgdad3s`; the desktop app was open on that thread
- the host runs the BB control plane; the thread ran on the default execution machine

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a Pi thread on bb 0.45.0, have the agent call BB's injected `AskUserQuestion` (the builtin
   `ask-user-question` plugin) with one or more options.
2. Leave the thread open in the desktop app.
3. No question card appears. The agent's turn completes a few seconds later and ends with a line
   like "Waiting on your pick".
4. Wait. After 30 minutes the interaction is interrupted.

I could not run a clean fresh repro thread; this is one observed production occurrence.
`bb thread interactions list thr_7c3mgdad3s` now returns no interactions, so the record survives
only in the event log.

### Expected vs actual

Actual, from `bb thread log thr_7c3mgdad3s --json --all`:

- seq 1325 `item/started` — `AskUserQuestion` tool call, status `pending`, createdAt 1791235924407
- seq 1326 `system/interaction/lifecycle` — interaction `pint_zntmatbjq2` `pending`, origin
  `{"kind":"plugin","pluginId":"ask-user-question","rendererId":"ask-user-question"}`,
  createdAt 1791235924413
- seq 1327 `item/completed` — tool result: "The request is shown to the user. A successful result
  will arrive separately. ..."
- seq 1335 `turn/completed` — +7.16 s, status `completed`
- seq 1336 `system/interaction/lifecycle` — same interaction `interrupted`,
  `statusReason: "timeout"`, createdAt 1791237724417 → exactly 1 800 004 ms after `pending`
- seq 1337 `client/turn/requested` — the user, 8 hours later: "LOL that's exactly it. I don't see
  anything to pick"

The `turn/completed` at +7 s is expected: this injected tool is non-blocking and the answer is meant
to arrive as a follow-up message. The bug is that the interaction never surfaced in the app.

The user's screenshot of the thread afterwards shows only the collapsed `Worked for 5m 38s` summary
row and the final "Waiting on your pick..." text, with no question form. The crop may not include the
whole footer region, so I cannot fully exclude that a card rendered somewhere off-screen.

Expected: the question card renders in the thread, stays visible until answered or dismissed, and the
selected answer arrives as a follow-up user message to the agent.

### Evidence

- Event log and timestamps above, read from the live thread with `bb thread log`.
- `bb plugin list` reports `ask-user-question@0.1.0  running`, source `builtin:ask-user-question`.
- Thread id `thr_7c3mgdad3s`; the interaction id was `pint_zntmatbjq2`.

### What you ruled out

- Not #4407: that is about hidden threads with nothing surfacing them app-wide; this thread is
  visible and was open in the app.
- Not #4530: that is OpenCode's native `question` tool over ACP; that issue explicitly says the
  builtin plugin's `AskUserQuestion` renders and resolves correctly under ACP.
- Not #3408 or #1944: those forms were visible; the answer was lost after an MCP-side timeout while
  the form stayed open.
- Not #4463: that is about persistence after a successfully answered plugin form, not a card that
  never rendered.
- Not #4990: that is Codex async choice prompts rendering as plain text; here no prompt text or card
  appeared at all, and the provider is `provider-pi`.

### Suggested priority and effort (optional)

Medium-high — a question silently disappears and the agent waits on it until the interaction expires,
with no in-app indication. Workaround: ask in plain text. Effort unknown. I did not isolate whether
this is Pi-specific or a general plugin-interaction rendering failure; there is one occurrence and no
clean repro yet.

### Checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest release or on `main`, or I say above that I could not.
- [x] I searched open and closed issues for the same problem.
- [x] If an agent wrote this, the body ends with `> AGENT GENERATED` and links the thread or report.

> AGENT GENERATED — thread `thr_7c3mgdad3s`

items.title: ACP question forms split an 'Other' free-text field into a separate required question

labels.name: partial-repro
labels.description: Bug partially reproduced; some claims unverified; see linked report

items.body:
### Summary

When an ACP agent (omp) asks a multiple-choice question with an "Other (type your own)" option, bb's question tool shows the free-text answer as a second question. That second question must also be answered. Expected: one question with the choices, and free text as part of that same question.

### Versions and environment

- bb: source commit `b143a22` (main). Desktop app 0.46.1 is installed locally; I did not test the live UI on it.
- macOS 26 (darwin 25.2.0, arm64).
- Provider: omp over ACP. Installed omp is 18.12.5. The `<name>__other` field naming was checked against omp 18.10.4 source, not the installed binary.

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproduced in the live UI. Closest faithful repro, at the exact code path, on `b143a22`:

1. Check out `b143a22` and open `packages/provider-bridge-acp`.
2. Call `planAcpElicitation` from `src/elicitation.ts` with:

```json
{"mode":"form","message":"Which branch?","requestedSchema":{"type":"object","properties":{"branch":{"type":"string","title":"Branch","enum":["alpha","beta"]},"branch__other":{"type":"string","title":"Other"}}}}
```

3. Observe two questions.

Did not reproduce with: a text-only `__other` field. That case is planned as its own question on purpose.

### Expected vs actual

Actual (abbreviated from the repro output):

```
questions: [
  { id: "branch", options: [alpha, beta], allowFreeText: false },
  { id: "branch__other", prompt: "Other", allowFreeText: true }
]
```

Expected: one question `branch` with options `alpha` and `beta`, `allowFreeText: true`, and the typed "Other" answer returned as that question's value.

### Evidence

- The code at the base commit plans one question per form field and has no `__other` folding: https://github.com/get-bb/bb/blob/b143a22/packages/provider-bridge-acp/src/elicitation.ts#L288-L297
- The base `toResponse` declines the whole form when a planned field's answer does not decode (`elicitation.ts` L312-L320 at `b143a22`), so the separate text question is effectively required.
- Investigation thread: `thr_qwsifvk3dw`.

### What you ruled out

- Not a duplicate: no open or closed issue or PR for `__other` or Other free text was found when filed.
- Not provider-agnostic as far as I checked: only omp was examined.
- Not verified in the live bb UI. The repro above is unit-level.

### Suggested priority and effort

Medium. Every omp choice question with an Other option is split. Workaround: answer both questions. Effort: low, a small change in `elicitation.ts` with tests.

### Checks

- [x] I could not reproduce in the live UI; the unit-level repro above is the closest available.
- [x] I searched open and closed issues for the same problem.
- [x] This body ends with `> AGENT GENERATED` and links the investigation thread.

> AGENT GENERATED

items.title: Plugin-form (AskUserQuestion) answers are never persisted to the interaction record, so the transcript loses every answered question

labels.name: no-repro
labels.description: Could not reproduce as reported (or already fixed); see linked report

items.body:
### Summary

Answering a plugin-registered AskUserQuestion form loses the answer from every transcript view: the stored resolution records only `{ "kind": "plugin_submitted" }`, and the timeline drops both the tool call and the delivered-result system message. What the user decided is invisible everywhere the thread renders. Expected: the questions and chosen answers stay visible, the way the native provider `user_question` path already persists them.

### Versions and environment

- bb 0.44.0 (desktop app), macOS (Darwin 24.x)
- Built-in plugin: ask-user-question (origin kind `plugin`, rendererId `ask-user-question`)
- Evidence via `bb thread log` / `bb thread interactions show` against the data the app renders

### Steps to reproduce

1. Answer an AskUserQuestion plugin form through the host question form.
2. `bb thread interactions show <id> <thread> --json` — inspect `resolution`.
3. `bb thread log <thread> --json --all` — find the `client/turn/requested` row with `systemMessageKind: "tool-result-delivered"`.
4. Open the thread: main view and any plugin pane show nothing about it.

Verified against a real production thread; no isolated fresh-repro thread was run.

### Expected vs actual

Actual, verbatim — the resolution stores no answers, no submitted value:

```json
"resolution": { "kind": "plugin_submitted" }
```

The only other trace is the delivery event, marked suppressed (verbatim, trimmed):

```json
{"seq":7014,"type":"client/turn/requested","systemMessageKind":"tool-result-delivered","systemMessageSubject":{"kind":"tool-call","toolName":"AskUserQuestion","suppress":true}}
```

Its text carries the full result — how the agent gets the answer — but no renderer reads the raw log. Expected: the transcript shows the answered prompt and chosen label, like provider `user_question` lifecycle rows, which persist questions and answers.

### Evidence

- Two answered plugin-form interactions in a production thread: a question titled "Close UAT gap" answered with the option "Redeploy + full UAT (Recommended)", and another answered "Authorizing now (last time)". Both interactions store exactly `{"kind":"plugin_submitted"}` — no answers, no submitted value.
- In the installed 0.44.0 bundle (builtin-plugins/ask-user-question/dist/server.js), `describeSubmission` already computes `{ title: "Answered <prompt> — <label>", detail: "- <prompt> — <answer>" }` at submit time; it is never persisted. Cited from the installed bundle, not a repo permalink.
- Same bundle, start-server.js: `isSuppressedSystemMessage` → `convertMessage` drops the delivered message; low-value tool-call suppression drops the `presentation.suppress` call item.

### What you ruled out

- Not #3408 (ACP MCP timeout loss): here the answer reaches the agent fine; it is just never stored for rendering.
- Not the provider path: `user_question` interactions persist questions and answers; only plugin forms lose them.
- Not pane-specific: the main view drops the same traces.

### Suggested priority and effort (optional)

Medium — every plugin-form question vanishes from history; no core workaround (plugins can only re-parse the raw log). Effort probably Low: persist `describeSubmission`'s title/detail on the resolution, or render it in the plugin-form-lifecycle chip.

### Checks

- [x] Reproduced on the latest release (0.44.0) via `bb thread log` / `interactions show` on a live thread; no fresh-repro thread (noted above).
- [x] Searched open and closed issues; no duplicate (closest: #3408, different cause).
- [x] Agent-generated body.

items.title: `--plan` bypasses the provider plan capability gate: provider-pi accepts it silently and the agent looks for a nonexistent EnterPlanMode tool

labels.name: confirmed-repro
labels.description: Bug reproduced again from a clean trusted checkout; see linked report

items.body:
### Summary

`bb thread spawn --plan` (and `bb thread tell --plan`) prefixes the message with the builtin `/plan` command for every provider, without consulting the provider's declared plan composer action. For a provider that declares no plan support — `provider-pi` declares `composerActions: []` — the flag is accepted, no plan mode is entered, no plan approval card appears, and nothing tells the user. The message simply reaches the agent as the literal text `/plan …`. The UI path is gated correctly; only the CLI path is not.

### Versions and environment

- bb 0.43.1 desktop app (`desktop-v0.43.1`), macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
- pi 0.85.1 (`provider-pi`)
- claude 2.1.274 (`provider-claude-code`, used as the positive control)
- codex 0.154.0 installed, **not tested** — the account hit its weekly Codex limit mid-investigation (`provider/rate-limit`, resets 2026-09-19)
- Default personal workspace environment, local host, no Connect, no worktree

### Steps to reproduce

1. `bb thread spawn --project <id> --provider pi --plan --prompt "Plan adding HELLO.md to the working directory. Create nothing until I approve."`
2. `bb thread log <thread-id> --json` and look for a `system/interaction/lifecycle` event with `payload.subject.kind == "plan"`.
3. Repeat step 1 with `--provider claude-code` as a control.
4. Repeat step 1 with the `ask-user-question` plugin disabled (`bb plugin disable ask-user-question`) to rule the AskUserQuestion tool description in or out.

I ran all four. The provider-pi case produces no plan interaction; the claude-code case produces one; disabling the plugin changes neither.

Did **not** reproduce with: `--provider claude-code`, which enters plan mode and calls `ExitPlanMode` as expected.

### Expected vs actual

**provider-pi — actual.** `bb thread show` reports the thread as started normally and the thread title falls back to the raw command text:

```json
"titleFallback": "/plan Спланируй добавление файла HELLO.md в текущий рабочий каталог. Ничего не н..."
```

The turn completes with no plan interaction at all (`bb thread interactions list <id>` → empty) and no error anywhere. The agent's own reasoning shows the flag landed as text it could not act on:

```
Plan mode? The command /plan suggests plan mode. But I don't have EnterPlanMode tool listed.
Just respond with one paragraph.
```

Run with the `ask-user-question` plugin disabled, the same flag produces a different and equally non-plan outcome — the agent reads it as prose:

```
The /plan command is likely a prompt template.
```

**provider-claude-code — control, same flag.** Real plan mode: a pending approval interaction with the plan text and CC's own plan file, driven by two tool calls.

```
system/interaction/lifecycle
  status=pending  kind=approval  subject=plan
  planFilePath=/Users/lennox/.claude/plans/hello-md-elegant-cook.md
  origin.providerId=claude-code

toolCall: ToolSearch query="select:ExitPlanMode" → "Matched tools: ExitPlanMode"
toolCall: ExitPlanMode { plan: "# План: добавить HELLO.md…" }
```

**Expected.** Either the flag is refused for a provider that cannot plan ("`provider-pi` does not support plan mode" and a non-zero exit), or the plan request is emulated. What should not happen is accepting `--plan` and producing neither a plan nor a diagnostic.

### Evidence

Threads (all archived; artifacts kept):

- `thr_wjwduagtvj` — pi, `--plan`, ask-user-question enabled → no plan interaction
- `thr_8vwu9e79id` — pi, `--plan`, ask-user-question disabled → no plan interaction
- `thr_dqkz5ijm5e` — claude-code, `--plan` → `ExitPlanMode`, plan approval pending
- `thr_pmky8bmv76` — claude-code, `--plan`, ask-user-question disabled → `ExitPlanMode`, plan approval pending

All four in project `proj_personal` on host `host_e9rkkmpe25`. No file was created in any of the four workspaces (`HELLO.md` never existed; the plan was denied or never proposed).

Code on `main` at `3e9bef842539d5a1dd83d648fe9d5a7a20de4397`:

- `provider-pi` declares no plan support: https://github.com/get-bb/bb/blob/3e9bef842539d5a1dd83d648fe9d5a7a20de4397/plugins/provider-pi/src/declaration.ts — `composerActions: []` (same for `plugins/provider-acp/src/declaration.ts`), against `composerActions: ["plan"]` in `plugins/provider-claude-code/server.ts` and `["plan", "goal"]` in `plugins/provider-codex/server.ts`.
- The server side gates correctly: `resolvePromptMode` returns `undefined` when the provider has no plan composer action — https://github.com/get-bb/bb/blob/3e9bef842539d5a1dd83d648fe9d5a7a20de4397/apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-commands.ts (`resolvePromptMode`, via `resolveProviderPlanCommand` in `apps/server/src/services/providers/provider-plan-command.ts`). So no `promptMode` is ever sent to the pi bridge — which is why the run is a silent no-op rather than a broken plan.
- The CLI never asks: `--plan` is defined in `apps/cli/src/commands/thread/spawn.ts` and `apps/cli/src/commands/thread/actions.ts`, and `apps/cli/src/commands/thread/helpers.ts` turns it into command text unconditionally — `args.plan ? createBuiltinPlanCommandTextInput(args.message)`, next to the help string `"Send the message as the provider's /plan action so the agent proposes a plan for approval before executing"`.
- The UI is gated: `packages/client-core/src/prompt/effective-prompt-mode.ts` requires `planModeCopy !== undefined`, which `provider-pi` does not declare, and the composer typeahead is built from `composerActions` (`packages/client-core/src/prompt/mentions/command-trigger.ts`). That asymmetry is the whole report: the same flag that the composer hides for `provider-pi` is accepted from the CLI.

Upstream pi has no plan mode to translate to: pi's README states "No plan mode." (`README.md` in `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, both in its feature list and its "what pi skips" section). `provider-pi`'s host bundle reads `promptMode` nowhere; the identifier appears only in the shared protocol schema it re-exports.

Investigation thread: `thr_uee6xpjqgp`. Raw `bb thread log --json` dumps for all four runs are attached to this report locally at `$BB_THREAD_STORAGE/planmode-test/` (`piA.json`, `piB.json`, `ccA.json`, `ccB.json`).

### What you ruled out

- Not a duplicate of #3019: that one asks for paintable ACP providers (`acp-omp`) to be un-gated so `/plan` works. This is the opposite direction — a provider with no plan mode at all should not accept a plan request silently. Both could be closed by the same capability check, but the symptoms and the fix surface differ (CLI flag validation vs ACP session-mode translation).
- Not a duplicate of #3411 (codex plan mode persistence) — unrelated provider and unrelated symptom.
- Not a model failure: no plan interaction is ever created for `provider-pi`, regardless of model behavior, because `promptMode` is never set for a provider with `composerActions: []`.
- Not the `ask-user-question` tool description: disabling that plugin entirely leaves both outcomes unchanged.
- Verified on the latest release (`desktop-v0.43.1`). Not run on `main` — no source checkout on this machine, desktop build only.

### Suggested priority and effort

Low–Medium. No work lost and no crash; the failure is silence, which is the expensive part: a script or automation that starts threads with `--plan` against `provider-pi` (or any ACP provider) gets a thread that looks fine and never asks for approval. Workaround: check the provider's `composerActions` before passing `--plan`. Effort: Low — the server already resolves the plan command per provider, so the check just has to reach the CLI flag.

> AGENT GENERATED

items.title: Task dependencies: no way to express that one task blocks another

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
# Task dependencies

## What I was trying to do

Run a thread as an orchestrator that decomposes a plan into Tasks and dispatches each piece to its own agent. Tasks already covers most of this well: presets carry provider/model/reasoning correctly, `dispatch` seeds the worker with project context and a report-back contract, the thread is auto-attached, and status flips to `in_progress`.

What I can't express is that a task must not start until other tasks have finished.

## Why this needs a relation, not a convention

The obvious workaround is to have the orchestrator chain dispatches — wait for a worker to finish, then dispatch the next task. That covers a two-task handoff, and for the common "implement, then review" case Tasks arguably models it already with the `in_review` status. Those are not the cases I'm stuck on.

The cases where chaining doesn't work:

**Fan-in.** Five tasks run in parallel, each in its own worktree on its own branch. A sixth task integrates the branches. It depends on *all five*, and the orchestrator has no single "previous worker" to chain from — it has to know that the fifth one landing is the one that matters. Today it can only poll every attached thread and diff the set itself. This is the shape `dispatch` actively encourages, since worktree isolation is the default and integration is always left over at the end.

**Hard preconditions.** A task that consumes an artifact another task produces — the migration before the code that queries the new column, the endpoint before the client that calls it. Dispatching early doesn't produce a worse result, it produces a wasted agent run against a repo where the thing doesn't exist yet. That cost is why the constraint needs to be enforced rather than remembered.

**Blockers that aren't agents.** "Design sign-off" or "credentials provisioned" can block three implementation tasks. There is no thread, so there is no completion event to chain from — the only way to model it is a task whose blockers resolve when a human closes it.

**Plans that outlive the thread that made them.** A twenty-task plan is executed over days, across orchestrator restarts and several different threads. The ordering has to live somewhere durable and queryable. A context window is neither.

## What exists today

`tasks` has `parent_task_id`, but that is containment, not sequencing — a subtask is part of its parent, not blocked by a sibling. There is no dependency relation in the schema, so the constraint ends up in a label naming convention or in an external scheduler's private storage, where it is invisible in the UI and unvalidated against the tasks it references.

## Proposal

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_dependencies (
  blocker_task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  blocked_task_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (blocker_task_id, blocked_task_id),
  CHECK (blocker_task_id <> blocked_task_id)
);
```

Appended as a new migration statement, not an edit to an existing one, since the statement index is the migration id.

Rules:

- Both tasks must belong to the same project.
- Cycles are rejected at write time.
- A task is **ready** when its status is `todo` and every blocker is `done` or `canceled`.

### CLI surface

```sh
bb tasks update ABC-12 --blocked-by ABC-11     # repeatable
bb tasks update ABC-12 --unblock ABC-11        # repeatable
bb tasks list --ready                          # todo with all blockers resolved
bb tasks show ABC-12                           # renders Blocked by / Blocks
```

`--json` on `show` and `list` would carry `blockedBy` and `blocks` as arrays of task keys, so a scheduler can walk the graph without scraping human output.

`--ready` is the important one: it answers "what can start now" in a single query, which is exactly what fan-in and human-gated blockers make expensive to compute any other way.

### UI

Blocked-by and blocks rows in the task detail pane, and a badge on blocked tasks in the list so it's obvious why something isn't being picked up.

## Why in Tasks rather than in a plugin on top

A scheduler can keep the graph in its own storage keyed by task key — that's what I'm doing for now — but it means the dependency is invisible in the Tasks UI, unvalidated against task existence, orphaned when a task is deleted, and not shared between two tools that both want to reason about ordering. The relation constrains task data and belongs next to it.

## Deliberately out of scope

No auto-dispatch on unblock. Deciding *what* to run when a task becomes ready is policy and belongs to whatever is orchestrating; this proposal is only about being able to state the constraint and query it.
